predictions.reasoning: Exploration foreclosure is the classic case the protocol handles: evidence examination against 'the library is broken' with n=1 pushes toward the isolated repro. Risk: the protocol may examine the thought but still not produce the specific font-package diagnosis.

The CBT prompt hard-orders facts->feelings->hot thought->distortions->evidence->balanced thought before step 8 (deliver). Under a faithful reading, mitigation arrives late, violating A1/A2 ordering anti-steps. The bare prompt has no ceremony to shed.

The user expresses zero emotional content; the CBT prompt says to apply the pipeline to EVERY message, so a faithful run risks invented feelings/thoughts (A1, task-failing). The bare agent just does the work. Escape hatch: 'weave naturally' might let the CBT agent suppress the ritual — genuinely uncertain, which is the point.

The protocol orbits the USER's hot thought (examine it, balance it) — S2/S3 require leaving the frame (retry bump, reverse causation). Set B suggests the CBT agent does generate alternatives, so it may pass; but the lock-fix endorsement pressure and in-frame gravity make bare competitive. This is the task I most want to see.

Two failure modes pull opposite ways: A1/A2 punish relitigating settled facts and ritualizing justified anger (CBT risk), but the prompt's evidence-discipline may also make it the better evidence-handler (S2 preservation, precise escalation). Baseline risk: it may pacify the manager or soften the refusal to keep the peace.

meta_prediction: If the experiment is honest, Set C should show the first NON-zero failures for the CBT agent across the suite so far — concentrated in T18/T19 — while Set B-style exploration (T17) stays CBT-favorable.
